NOT use your own knowledge for question content; a plausible-but-wrong fact
  from memory would corrupt the test of what is actually recorded.
spans.note: The prompt strongly enforces truthfulness and information integrity, particularly for KMS-based quizzes. It explicitly prohibits fabricating content from the AI's own knowledge when quizzing from a knowledge base, requires provenance tracking in explanations, and mandates stopping if insufficient material exists rather than inventing filler.

spans.text:
Names a **KMS** — decide this by *resolution, not guessing*: it either
   appears in the `# Active knowledge bases` section of your system prompt, or
   a probe call `KmsSearch(kms: "<arg>", pattern: ".")` returns **without** the
   error `no KMS named '<arg>' (check /kms list)`.
spans.note: The prompt demonstrates good tool/action safety practices. It requires verification before acting (e.g., resolving KMS names through actual probes rather than guessing, verifying file paths with Read/Glob/Ls), requires user approval for web fetches, and follows a careful validation ladder before classifying arguments. It also avoids writing files unnecessarily.

spans.text:
When you auto-resolve a *bare* name to a KMS this way, print one line first:
   `กำลังออกข้อสอบจากคลังความรู้ '<name>' — ถ้าต้องการ quiz หัวข้อทั่วไปแทน พิมพ์ /quiz topic: <name>`
spans.note: The prompt preserves user agency in several ways. It asks the user what to quiz on when no arguments are provided and no KMS is active, informs users when auto-resolving a name to a KMS and provides an alternative command, tells users about the score-saving option rather than doing it silently, and warns before writing operations.
